texts.value: Functions both as a mechanical stabilizer (via LIM domains) of focal adhesions, and as a sensor component for muscle cell damage (via N-terminus) (PubMed:23427270). Regulates, stabilizes and maintains posterior lateral mechanosensory (PLM) synaptic branch extension and new synapse formation and growth during larval development (PubMed:25252943)
Interacts with dyc-1 (PubMed:18094057, PubMed:23427270). Interacts with glh-1 and glh-3 (PubMed:12435362)

Shuttles between dense bodies and M lines (PubMed:18094057, PubMed:23427270). Localizes to nucleus in body wall muscle cells. Highly mobile in cytoplasm. Mobility seems to depend on atn-1 (PubMed:23427270)
Expressed in neurons and body wall muscle (PubMed:18094057, PubMed:23427270, PubMed:25252943). Expressed in pharyngeal, enteric and uterine muscles and in spermatheca (PubMed:25252943)
Expressed in neurons and muscle throughout development
The LIM domains are sufficient for the role in PLM synaptogenesis
RNAi-mediated knock-down of isoform a in a dys-1/hlh-1 double mutant background reduces muscle degeneration
Produced by alternative splicing of isoform a

citation.title: Genome sequence of the nematode C. elegans: a platform for investigating biology.
The GLH proteins, Caenorhabditis elegans P granule components, associate with CSN-5 and KGB-1, proteins necessary for fertility, and with ZYX-1, a predicted cytoskeletal protein.
DYC-1, a protein functionally linked to dystrophin in Caenorhabditis elegans is associated with the dense body, where it interacts with the muscle LIM domain protein ZYX-1.
ZYX-1, the unique zyxin protein of Caenorhabditis elegans, is involved in dystrophin-dependent muscle degeneration.
The conserved LIM domain-containing focal adhesion protein ZYX-1 regulates synapse maintenance in Caenorhabditis elegans.
